Updated assessment incorporating Beige Book and SLOOS:
- Policy stance remains cautious-hawkish: inflation still elevated and labor markets tight enough to justify the March 25 bp hike to 4.75–5.00% and ongoing QT.
- Beige Book reports broadly flat-to-slight growth across districts, with softer discretionary consumer spending, mixed-to-weak manufacturing, subdued housing activity, and notable CRE softness (especially office). New York and San Francisco districts highlight ongoing housing market strains, while some districts (e.g., Boston) still report above-average wage growth, keeping underlying price pressure risks alive even as wage and price gains show signs of gradual moderation elsewhere.
- SLOOS and Beige Book are consistent: banks are tightening standards; loan demand is weakening across C&I and CRE; and firms cite reduced financing needs for capex, inventories, and M&A. This points to a clearer drag on hiring and investment ahead.
- Financial stability backstops reduce tail risks, but they don’t offset the growth headwind from tighter lending and softer demand.

Net effect: compared with the prior assessment, the Beige Book tilts the outlook modestly more negative for growth and risk assets, with only incremental relief on inflation momentum. Adjusting sentiment slightly lower.
